verdict.rationale: Daily's large-calls docs say each participant receives tracks from at most 12 others at a time, which implies server-side selective forwarding. Its global mesh network routes media to cut latency. Neither source explicitly names an SFU or a per-participant subscription mechanism. Missing for 10: explicit SFU/relay architecture documentation, a documented track-subscription API letting participants choose which tracks they receive, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, media routes through a selective forwarding unit or relay that delivers only the tracks each participant subscribes to

citations.quote: These calls can support up to 1,000 participants with all cameras on, with each participant viewing (and receiving tracks from) at most 12 other participants at a time.
In many cases, this reduces the latency, packet loss, and jitter — improving the overall call experience for end users around the globe.
